translations.text:
✠
By the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, we begin printing the Book of Before and After, the Cycle, the Collection, the Treasury, and the Chant of the Helps, together with the Book of Psalms, according to the order of Saint Gabriel and Saint Abraham of the Upper Monastery.
Printed at the press of Saint Narsai the Teacher, in Thrissur, a city in southern India, in the year of our Lord 1960.
1960.

The Book of Before and After.
The order of evening prayer for ordinary days, for the week of the first choir.
Instructions.
First the chief officiant, the bishop, begins. If he is not present, the archdeacon begins. If there is no archdeacon, the priest whose ordination is earliest among the priests in his choir begins. Know also that if the day's prayer belongs to the first choir, its beginning is to be in the first choir; if it belongs to the second choir, in the second. This is determined from the Cycle, except during Lent. If the chant of the Sunday vigil is “The Lord reigns,” it belongs to the first choir. If it is “Then Moses sang praise,” it belongs to the second choir. Thus, if Sunday belongs to the first choir, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday also belong to the first choir, while Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday belong to the second choir. The same applies to the feasts and commemorations that fall on those days. The reverse applies if Sunday belongs to the second choir.
“Glory to God in the highest.” Repeat three times. “And on earth peace and good hope to humankind, at all times and forever. Amen.”
They say: “Give the blessing, my lord.” They continue with the chant: “Our Father in heaven,

may your name be hallowed; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven. Heaven and earth are filled with the greatness [?] of your glory. The watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.
Our Father in heaven, may your name be hallowed; may your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today the bread we need, and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. Do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours are the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever and ever. Amen.
The chief officiant continues: “Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.”
They respond: “From everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.”
“Our Father in heaven, may your name be hallowed; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven. Heaven and earth are filled with the greatness of your glory. The watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.”
The deacon says: “Let us pray. Peace be with us.”
Prayer.
“Let us give thanks, Lord, to your divinity and worship your lordship, and let us offer constant, unceasing glory to your glorious Trinity at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.”
They respond [?]: “Amen.”
For Monday evening, of the first choir.
Psalm sections.
“In the Lord I have taken refuge. How can you say to my soul?”
“Lord, who may dwell in your tent?” See page 249.
Then the priest says the prayer of incense: “Let us offer praise to your glorious Trinity at all times, forever. Amen.”
Or this prayer:
“Christ, who received the blood of the martyrs on the day they were killed, receive this incense from my feeble hands, through the grace of your compassion, forever. Amen.”
(He makes the sign of the cross over the censer and puts incense in it.)

And he says the prayer “To you, Lord”: And for all your help and kindness toward us, which cannot be repaid, we will thank you and praise you without ceasing in your crowned church, full of every help and every blessing. For you are the Lord and Creator of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever. And they answer: Amen.

Then both choirs say together: You, Lord of all, we thank; and you, Jesus Christ, we praise. For you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the Savior of our souls. (The verse inside the church.) I rejoiced when they said to me, “We are going to the house of the Lord.” (Outside the church they say:) You are everywhere, O God; accept our supplication.

You, Lord of all, we thank; and you, Jesus Christ, we praise. For you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the Savior of our souls. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, from eternity to eternity. Amen and amen. You, Lord of all, we thank; and you, Jesus Christ, we praise. For you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the Savior of our souls.

And the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

Prayer of the first opening chant. You, my Lord, are truly the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls and the constant guardian of our lives. To you, my Lord, we owe thanks, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all….. And they [?]: Amen. They say the opening chant in the first choir.

First opening chant. Save us, Lord, for the good person is no more.
Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. Save us, Lord, for the good person is no more. (1) And faithfulness has vanished from the earth. People speak empty words, each with his neighbor, with deceitful lips. They speak with a double heart. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and tongues that speak boastfully, those who say, “We will make our tongue great,” and the lips

(1) This is how they begin all the opening chants.

They are ours; who is our lord? Because of the plundering of the poor and the groaning of the afflicted, now I will rise, says the Lord, and I will bring salvation openly.

Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.

The members of the choir whose leader begins respond: Hallelujah, hallelujah. The members of the other choir respond: Hallelujah.

The leader of the first choir begins the antiphons in this way: “Save us, Lord, for the good have disappeared.” The whole choir joins him in unison: “Look, the good have disappeared and come to an end.” Likewise, the other choir sings the following antiphon, and so on.... In this way they complete all the opening chants and all the antiphons of the first and second choirs, on every day of the ordinary weeks.

Antiphons of the first choir.
To the tune of “Look, he has taken me captive.”

Save us, Lord, for the good have disappeared.
Look, the good have disappeared, the righteous have come to an end, and the godly have perished. There is no one upright among human beings. Everyone speaks with a double heart, and each speaks to his neighbor with divided lips. Envy, deceit, and slander fill our inner selves. Love, which is the foremost commandment, has been uprooted from our minds. We greatly fear because of this that you may destroy us in your anger. For your justice has remained silent toward us and made room for your grace. Our Lord, have mercy on us.

The Lord is faithful in his words.
Our Savior promised life to those who cherish his love, and enriched them with knowledge of him. He filled them with the wisdom of his power and taught them to pray at all times: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your kingdom come to us. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us the bread we need, and do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours are the kingdom, the power, and the glory.

Glory....
Mary, who gave birth to the medicine of life for Adam’s children, through your intercession may we find refuge. Trusting in the prayers of Saint John, may we overcome the evil one and his power, and through the prayers of the prophets, apostles, martyrs, fathers, and teachers.

And through the prayer of our holy father, and of the confessors and Saint George, and through the great power of the cross and the holiness of the holy Church, let us plead with Christ to show mercy and compassion to our souls.

The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The prayer for “Lord, I have called to you,” in the second choir.

For your mercy, our Lord and our God, and for the care your will provides for us, we are bound to give thanks, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all...

They respond: Amen.

And they say:
Lord, I have called to you; answer me. Hear my words and accept my prayer.
Lord, I have called to you; answer me.
Hear my words and accept my prayer like incense before you.
May the offering of my hands be like the evening offering.
Set a guard over my mouth, Lord, and a guard over my lips,
so that my heart does not turn toward an evil word,
and I do not do deeds of injustice.
Let me not share fellowship with wicked men.
Let a righteous person teach me and rebuke me.
Let the oil of the wicked not anoint my head,
for my prayer is against their wickedness.
Their judges were held back at the side of the rock,
and he heard my words, which were pleasant.
Like a plowshare that splits the earth,
their bones were scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
But I have lifted my eyes to you, Lord,
and I have trusted in you; do not cast away my soul.
Protect me from the hands of the proud,
who have hidden snares for me.
Let the unjust fall together into their traps,
until I have passed by.

With my voice I called to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.
I laid my plea before him,
and made my distress known before him.
When my spirit was overwhelmed, you knew my paths.
On the road where I walked, they hid snares for me.
I looked to the right and saw that there was no one who knew me.
My refuge was lost to me, and there was no one who cared for my soul.
I cried out to you, Lord, and said:
You are my hope and my portion in the land of the living.
Listen to my plea, for I have been brought low.

Good. Rescue me from my persecutors, because they are stronger than I am. Bring my soul out of prison so that I may give thanks to your name. Your righteous ones will wait for me until you reward me.

Your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my paths. I have sworn and confirmed that I will keep your righteous judgments. I have been greatly humbled; Lord, give me life according to your word. Accept the words of my mouth, Lord, and teach me your judgments. My soul is always in your hands, and I have not forgotten your law. Sinners have laid traps for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments. I have inherited your testimony forever, because it is the delight of my heart. I have turned my heart to carry out your commandments forever in truth.

Praise the Lord, all you peoples, and praise him, all you nations. For his grace has been mighty toward us. Truly, the Lord is forever. Glory... Forever... Both choirs finish together: Lord, I have called upon you; answer me. Listen to my words and accept my prayer. And the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

Prayer for the opening chant that follows, in the latter choir. Hear, our Lord and our God, the prayer of your servants in your compassion, and accept the petition of your worshipers in your mercy. Have compassion on our sinfulness in your grace and your mercies, healer of our bodies and good hope of our souls, Lord of all... And they [?]: Amen.

They say the opening chant that follows in the latter choir.

The opening chant that follows. Lord, who will dwell in your tent? Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And who will abide on your holy mountain? The one who walks without blemish and does what is right, who speaks truth in his heart and is not deceitful with his tongue, who does no evil to his companion and accepts no bribe against his neighbor. The one who provokes anger is despised in his eyes, but he honors those who fear the Lord. Glory... Forever...

The members of the choir of the one who begins respond: Hallelujah, hallelujah. And they repeat.

The members of the other choir: Alleluia. They begin the following responses in the same way as the preceding ones.

The following responses. To the tune of “He who knows thoughts.”

He who exists from before the ages. Compassionate Father, merciful Son, and hovering Spirit, who sanctifies the unclean: sanctify our bodies and souls, and have mercy on us.

Holy and awesome is his name. May the declarations of holiness and praises of the heavenly assemblies, together with the supplication of the Son at the Father's right hand, plead with your justice on our behalf; and have mercy on us.

Glory... O Mary, mother of the King, the King of kings, plead with Christ, who shone forth from your womb, that he may have compassion on us in his grace and make us worthy of his kingdom.

Forever... Through the prayers of your saints, Christ our Savior—the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and all the righteous—protect the assembly of your worshipers from every harm.

Let us say... Our holy father, be our guide in upright conduct that pleases your Lord, so that through your prayers we may be helped and may share delight with you.

(The deacon puts on the stole, fastens the belt, and stands in an orderly manner before the sanctuary.) He recites the litany in the first choir: “Father of mercies.” (See page 411.) When it is finished, he adds: “Let us entrust our souls and one another's to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.” They respond: “To you, Lord our God.”

The priest prays in the first choir: “To you, Lord, mighty God, we entrust our bodies and souls. From you, our Lord and our God, we ask forgiveness of debts and sins. Grant it to us in your grace and mercy, as you always do, Lord of all...”

The deacon who proclaimed the litany says: “Raise your voices, and praise the living God, all you people.” They say in a simple tone: “Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.”

Glory... Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One:

Have mercy on us. Forever...
Holy God, holy mighty one, holy immortal one, have mercy on us.
And the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

Prayer after “Holy God.”
Holy, glorious, mighty, and immortal one, who dwells among the holy ones and whose will finds rest in them: we implore you, my Lord, turn toward us, have compassion, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all...
And they answer: Amen.

And the deacon who made the proclamation says: Bless, my lord. Bow your heads for the laying on of hands and receive the blessing.
And the superior says: May Christ make your ministry radiant in the kingdom of heaven.
And he continues with the prayer: As our souls agree in the one perfect faith in your glorious Trinity, may we all, in one accord of love, be worthy to offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship at all times, Lord of all.
And they answer: Amen.

And they say the evening anthem, as prescribed in the Kashkul; it is the anthem for the mysteries of the day. Glory... A supplement suited to the tune, or this one, to “By the Blessed Martyrs.”

It is said at the beginning of every week. They begin with the first choir.
I waited expectantly for the Lord. The poor shall eat and be satisfied.
The body of Christ and his precious blood are on the holy altar. With reverence and love, let us all approach him, and with the angels acclaim him: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God.
Repeat. Glory...
Christ, refuge and sure hope of those in distress, be a wall, my Lord, for those who worship you, and protect them from the evil one. Heal and bind up their wounds through the compassion of your divinity, merciful one who forgives sins.
And the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

Prayer of the signs, in the following choir.
Have compassion on us in your grace, you who are compassionate, and turn toward us, you who are full of mercy; and do not, my Lord, neglect

your watchfulness and care from us, for our hope and trust are in you at all times and seasons, Lord of all.... They respond: Amen.

Letters. Blessed are those whose way is blameless. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are those who keep his testimony and seek him with their whole heart. They have done no wrong, but have walked in his ways. You commanded that your commandments should be kept diligently. Oh, that my ways were set right, so that I might keep your commandments! Then I would not be ashamed when I kept all your commandments. I will thank you with an upright heart when I learn your righteous judgments. I will keep your commandments; do not abandon me forever. How can a young man make his way pure? By keeping your commandments. With my whole heart I have sought you; do not let me stray from your commandments. I have hidden your words in my heart so that I may not sin against you. Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your commandments. With my lips I have recounted all your righteous judgments. I have loved the way of your testimony more than all riches. I have reflected on your commandments and learned your ways. I have reflected on your law so that I may not forget your words.

Glory... Forever... They respond: Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. They follow this with: Our Father in heaven, with its concluding formula, as at the beginning. When it is finished, the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

Prayer. May your holy name, our Lord and our God, be glorified; may your divinity be worshiped, your lordship honored, your greatness celebrated, and your being exalted. May the eternal mercies of your glorious Trinity pour over your people and the sheep of your pasture at all times, Lord of all... They respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

Conclusion. In heaven and on earth, blessed is your divinity, my Lord, and worshiped is your lordship. Holy, glorious, glorified, high, and exalted is the worshiped and glorified name of your glorious Trinity, at all times, Lord

of all … And they respond: Amen. They then continue with the hymn of the martyrs for the evening of the day:
“Holy martyrs, pray.” See page 420.

Prayer after the evening hymn of the martyrs.

Prayer. To you, who exalts his church, crowns those who love him, gives victory to his champions, and helps his saints in their glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine struggles, we make supplication. Turn toward us, my Lord; have compassion and mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all.
And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

Another prayer. Through the prayers of your saints, our Lord and our God, be gracious to us. Through the petitions of your faithful ones, remove our sins and forgive our shortcomings. Make our enemies peaceful, raise our departed, and make us worthy of the splendid glory of your kingdom, together with the upright and righteous who fulfill your will in Jerusalem above, Lord of all.
And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

They then continue with the prayer for help, which is said only in church.

Prayer. May the help of your mercy, my Lord, the great assistance of your grace, the hidden and glorious power of your glorious Trinity, and your right hand, full of mercy and compassion, shelter and accompany your worshipers in their weakness, from your holy house, which is full of every help and every blessing, through the prayers of all the saints who please you, Lord of all …
And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

They then continue: With your blessing, our Lord and our God, may your servants be blessed, and through the care of your will may your worshipers be protected. May the constant peace of your divinity, my Lord, and the enduring peace of your lordship reign among your people and in your church throughout all the days of the world, Lord of all …
And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

(And if there are many priests, let each one of them say one of the following prayers, according to the seniority of his ordination.

After every prayer that is said, they respond: “Amen. Bless, my lord.”

Another prayer. May the blessing of the one who blesses all, the peace of the one who brings peace to all, the compassion of the one who has compassion on all, and the protection of our worshipful God be with us, among us, and around us, and protect us from the evil one and his forces, at all times and seasons, Lord of all…

Another prayer. May we be blessed by your blessing, our Lord and our God, and protected by your care. May your power come to our aid, and your help accompany us. May your right hand shield us, and your peace reign among us. May your cross be a high wall and a place of refuge for us, and may we hide beneath its wings from the evil one and his forces, at all times and [?], Lord of all…

Another prayer. Blessed, Lord, are the mercies of your grace, and worthy of worship are the promises of your lordship, which always teach us to look to you and glory in you, and not to give up our hope in you, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…

Another prayer. May your blessing, our Lord and our God, rest upon your people, and may your compassion be continually upon us, weak and sinful as we are, you who are our good hope, our refuge full of mercy, and the one who forgives offenses and sins, Lord of all…

Another prayer. May the peace of the Father be with us, and the love of the Son among us. May the Holy Spirit guide us according to his will, and may his mercies and compassion be upon us, at all [?] and seasons, Lord of all…

Another prayer. May your peace, Lord, dwell in us, and your harmony rule within us, and your love increase among us, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…

Another prayer. Protect us with your right hand, Lord, and shelter us beneath your wings. May your help accompany us all the days of our lives, Lord of all…

Another prayer. Give us, Lord, lasting peace, love, and a love of learning, life, blessings, and joys, and food that will not fail us, all the days of our lives, Lord of all…

Another. Be a guardian who never sleeps over the fold where your sheep dwell, so that it may not be harmed by wolves thirsting for the blood of your flock. For you are a sea that never runs dry, Lord of all...

Another. Bless us with your blessings, our Lord, and surround us with the wall of your care. Do not deprive us of good things, and give us a place in the bridal chamber of your light, Lord of all...

Another. Come, my Lord, to our aid in your compassion, and reveal yourself for our salvation in your mercy. Guide our steps along the paths of righteousness all the days of our lives, Lord of all...

Another. May your grace dawn upon us, my Lord, when your justice judges us. May your mercies come to our aid on the day when your majesty shines forth, Lord of all...

Another. May your blessing, your grace, and your right hand, full of mercy and compassion, shelter and remain over the congregation of your worshipers, who call upon you and plead with you at all times and seasons, Lord of all...

Another. Bless, my Lord, in your grace, and protect [?] in your mercy the congregation of believers who trust in you, call upon your holy name, and plead with you at all times, Lord of all.

Another. Be with us always in your mercy, my Lord, and lead us according to the will of your divinity all the days of our lives, Lord of all...

Another. May a blessing of mercy, my Lord, from the treasury of mercy, through the angel of mercy, be sent from God, who is abundant in mercy, and poured out upon the congregations of those who praise you, who continually call upon your holy name and look and wait for mercy and for the salvation that comes from you, Lord of all...

And they add: The prayer, my Lord, of the holy Virgin, the petition of the blessed Mother, and the pleading and entreaty of her who is full of grace:

May our blessed Lady Mary, the great power of the victorious cross, divine help, and the intercession of Saint John the Baptist, of the blessed apostles, of the illustrious fathers who proclaimed righteousness and sowed peace in creation, of our pure and holy father Mar Aba the Catholicos, of Saint Stephen, the first of the martyrs, of the mighty warrior Saint George, the illustrious martyr, of Saint So-and-so ..., of blessed Saint Eugene and his entire spiritual company, of Shmuni and her sons, and of all our Lord’s martyrs and saints, always be for us a high wall and a strong refuge, to redeem, deliver, rescue, and protect our bodies and souls from the evil one and his forces, at all times and seasons, Lord of all ... . And they answer: Amen.

Then they conclude with the following refrain. The priest takes the cross in his right hand, stands on the southern side, turns his face toward the people, and says: Bless, my lord. With your permission. And they answer: By the command of Christ our Lord, and glory to his holy name. The people bow their heads.

He then adds the concluding prayer: Glory to you, Jesus, our victorious King, the radiance of the eternal Father, begotten without a beginning, above times and created things. We have no hope or expectation except you, the Creator. Through the prayers of the righteous and the chosen, who have pleased you from the beginning, grant pardon for our sins, forgiveness for our offenses, deliverance from our afflictions, and an answer to our requests. Bring us to your glorious light, and protect us by your living sign from every harm, hidden and manifest, (Christ, the hope of our nature), now ♱ and at all times and forever and ever.

He makes the sign of the cross over the people, extending his hand upward toward the west and bringing it toward the east. Then he extends it toward the southern side and moves it toward the northern side, so that the consecration rests upon the northern side, which is the side [?]

The left side of the congregation. And they respond: May Christ hear your prayers; may Christ glorify your priesthood in the kingdom of heaven.

Another. May the prayer of your weak servants be accepted, our Lord and our God, before the judgment seat of your divinity. May this gathering of ours please the will of your lordship, so that by grace we may receive from you health of body, protection of the soul, abundant sustenance, (pardon for debts and forgiveness of sins), and, my Lord, lasting tranquility, enduring peace, and harmony in love that neither passes away nor dissolves among us, throughout the whole time that this world endures. (Christ, the hope of our nature,) now... ♱

Another. Blessed is God forever, and praised is his holy name from generation to generation. From him we ask, and to the overflowing sea of his compassion we make supplication, that he may make us worthy of the splendid glory of his kingdom, of delight with his holy angels, of confidence before him, and of standing at his right hand in Jerusalem above, by his grace and his mercies. (Christ, the hope of our nature,) now... ♱

Another. May God, the Lord of all, in whose house we have gathered and before whose majesty we have prayed, with great hope in his compassion, hear our prayer in his kindness and accept our petition in his pity. May he wash and cleanse the filth of our debts and our sins with the abundant hyssop of his compassion. May he give rest to the souls of our departed in the glorious dwellings of his kingdom, and sprinkle upon us all the dew of his goodness. May the right hand of his providence shelter us and all creatures, by his grace and his mercies. (Christ, the hope of our nature,) now... ♱

Another. May God, the Lord of all, who has placed his praises in our mouths, his songs on our tongues, his melodies in our throats, thanksgiving to him on our lips, and faith in him in our hearts, hear our prayers, accept our petitions, be pleased with our supplications, (pardon our debts,) and grant us what we ask.

Good and blameless. And from the great treasury of his compassion may he pour out his mercy and grace upon us and upon the whole world in its entirety: (Christ, the tomb of our nature) now… ♱

Another. May the name of God, the Lord of all, who orders the times and seasons, be praised among us. May the right hand of his providence and compassion shelter us, weak and sinful as we are, and the whole world in its entirety, and the holy Church and her children, and our fathers, our masters, our teachers, and our departed, and the departed who have left and passed away from among us, and our entire brotherhood in Christ: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱

Another. Glory to God, honor to the angels, shame to Satan, worship to the cross, exaltation to the Church, resurrection to the departed, acceptance to the repentant, release to prisoners, health and healing to the sick and infirm, and great tranquility and peace to the four quarters of the world. And upon us also, weak and sinful as we are, may the grace and mercy of our worshipful God come, shelter us, overflow, remain, and reign continually: (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱

Another. (By the right hand of your lordship, our Father in heaven): Bless us all, my Lord, and protect us all, and help us all, and support and shelter us all. Raise the departed of us all, and shelter us all with your right hand. May your mercy and grace overflow upon us all, and may praise, honor, thanksgiving, worship, and unceasing gratitude rise to you from the mouths of us all: (Christ, the tomb of our nature) now… ♱

Another. May God, the Lord of all, bless our assembly by his grace, and protect our order through the overflowing abundance of his compassion, and answer our petitions from his treasury; and upon the whole world in its entirety, and upon

The holy Church and her children; and upon this land and its inhabitants; and upon this monastery and those who dwell in it; and upon all of us together: may the grace and mercies of our good God come and be poured out continually. (Christ, the hope of our nature) now… ♱

They then continue with the creed of the three hundred and eighteen fathers, the bishops who assembled at Nicaea, a city of Bithynia, in the time of the victorious Emperor Constantine. The reason for their assembly was the wickedness of Arius. According to the custom current among the children of our holy and apostolic Church of the East—a custom that has long been current from ancient times and has extended down to our own days through the tradition and transmission of the ancients who were deeply versed in contemplation of divine truth—we begin to recite the rule of faith of Nicaea as follows:

Truly and without doubt, we believe in one God, the Father Almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the firstborn of all creation, who was begotten of his Father before all ages and was not made; true God from true God, of the same nature as his Father, through whose hands the ages were established and everything was created. For us human beings and for our salvation, he came down from heaven, took flesh through the Holy Spirit, and became human. He was conceived and born of the Virgin Mary. He suffered and was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate. He was buried and rose on the third day, as it is written. He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of his Father. He will come again to judge the dead and the living. And in one Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, the life-giving Spirit. And in one holy, apostolic, catholic Church.

And we acknowledge one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and the resurrection of our bodies, and life forever and ever. Amen.

…

For Tuesday evening of the first week.

Psalm sections. To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul. To you, Lord, I have cried; my God, do not be silent toward me. See page 261.

(For the note concerning the prayers, opening chants, and responses, see Monday of the first week, page 1.)

First opening chant. Hear, holy Lord, and look upon my petition. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah. And listen to the prayer [?], which does not come from deceitful lips. Let my judgment come from your presence, and let your eyes see what is right. You have examined my heart and visited me at night; you have tested me and found no wrongdoing in me. Nor have human deeds passed over my mouth in the speech of lips. Rather, you have kept me from my evil paths. You have supported my steps in your paths, so that my footsteps do not slip. I have called upon you because you have answered me.

Glory… Forever…

First responses. To “Light and Son of Light.”

“Hear, God, and have mercy on me.” You who hear and do not neglect, who answer, redeem, and rescue: hear our petition, my Lord, and in your mercy grant our requests.

“The Lord is faithful in his words.” Our Lord, you have said that everyone who knocks at the door of my lordship will have the door opened to him, and his requests will be granted.

Glory… May the prayer of the Virgin Mary, the mother of Christ, be a wall for us and protect us from the evil one.

Forever… Prophets and apostles, martyrs, priests, and teachers: may your prayer be a wall for us.
